item.title: Mongolia becomes new donor to World Bank's fund for poorest countries
item.description: The World Bank Group said on Saturday that Mongolia has become a new donor to the International Development Association fund for the poorest countries, after previously spending nearly three decades as a recipient of IDA funding.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The World Bank Group said on Saturday that Mongolia has become a new donor to the International Development Association fund for the poorest countries, after previously spending nearly three decades as a recipient of IDA funding. The development lender said that Mongolia's parliament approved a 4.8 billion tugrik ($1.3 million) contribution to the latest IDA funding round, marking a milestone in the country's development journey. Since becoming a World Bank member country in 1991, Mongolia has received more than $1.62 billion in development financing, including IDA support for transport, rural development, health and education. Mongolia graduated from IDA support in July 2020, becoming a client of the World Bank's main lending arm for middle-income countries, the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development. "Mongolia’s contribution to IDA21 marks an important milestone in our longstanding partnership with the World Bank and reflects our commitment to international solidarity," Mongolian Finance Minister Mendsaikhan Zagdjav said in a statement released by the World Bank. "Having benefited firsthand from IDA’s support, we recognize the vital role of concessional financing in helping countries reduce poverty, build resilience, and expand opportunities. As we continue to advance Mongolia's own development priorities, we are proud to support other countries in pursuing theirs."

item.title: Bruins escape 2-goal hole, emerge with win over Ducks
item.description: Elias Lindholm scored to break a third-period tie, capping a two-point performance as the visiting Boston Bruins registered a come-from-behind 4-2 victory over the Anaheim Ducks on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Elias Lindholm scored to break a third-period tie, capping a two-point performance as the visiting Boston Bruins registered a come-from-behind 4-2 victory over the Anaheim Ducks on Friday. David Pastrnak netted one goal and one assist for the Bruins, who scored four unanswered goals, three on the power play, to run their winning streak to four games. Frederic Brunet potted his first career NHL goal, Matthew Poitras added a tally, and Pavel Zacha and James Hagens each logged two assists. Bruins goaltender Michael DiPietro made 25 saves to earn his first NHL victory in his sixth game and fourth start. Tim Washe and Beckett Sennecke scored for the Ducks, who squandered a 2-0 lead and have dropped their second game in a row. Goalie Lukas Dostal stopped 18 shots. While the Bruins converted three of their four power-play opportunities, the Ducks were blanked on five chances with the extra skater. Anaheim also mustered only four shots on goal in the third period. After watching his team erase a 2-0 deficit, Lindholm put Boston on top at 8:18 of the third period with a tap-in tally set up by Zacha while on a power play. Poitras added an insurance goal eight minutes later when he finished a 2-on-1 rush on a setup from Hagens. Anaheim tallied twice late in the first period. Washe opened the scoring with 37.3 seconds remaining in the frame, finding the twine with his long shot from the point that made it through a screen and DiPietro's legs. Sennecke doubled the lead 21 seconds later, notching his fifth of the season by finishing a three-way passing play. Brunet, a 2022 fifth-round draft choice, halved Boston's deficit at 3:15 of the second period. He sent a long shot from the blue line that made it through the maze of traffic for his milestone marker. Pastrnak tied the clash with another man-advantage goal at 3:26 of the third period, pouncing on a loose puck during a scramble for his third of the campaign. Pastrnak took sole possession of the fourth spot on the Bruins' all-time goals list with his 423rd career tally, passing Brad Marchand. He trails only Johnny Bucyk (545 goals), Phil Esposito (459) and Patrice Bergeron (427). --Field Level Media

item.title: BOJ may need to tighten faster if inflation beats forecast, IMF says
item.description: The Bank of Japan is "doing the right thing" by normalising monetary policy and may need to raise interest rates faster if inflation rises more than expected, a senior International Monetary Fund official told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Leika Kihara
item.content:encoded: The Bank of Japan is "doing the right thing" by normalising monetary policy and may need to raise interest rates faster if inflation rises more than expected, a senior International Monetary Fund official told Reuters. Japan must also clarify how it plans to fund its big spending plans and lay out a medium-term fiscal framework to ease market concerns about fiscal risks, said Krishna Srinivasan, director of the IMF's Asia and Pacific Department. "I would say that they are doing the right thing at this point," Srinivasan said on the BOJ's efforts to lift its policy rate towards levels deemed neutral to the economy. "If inflation rises faster than expected, you have to start tightening faster because you don't want inflation expectations to get un-anchored. It's data dependent," he said in an interview on Friday. The remarks came ahead of the BOJ's key policy meeting later this month, when it [USN:L4N45S011 TEXT:"could keep rates steady"] but drop hawkish hints that would reinforce dominant market expectations of a December hike. Inflationary pressures from the Middle East conflict and brisk AI-demand were among key themes discussed by policymakers gathering for this week's annual IMF meetings in Bangkok. BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda, who attended the IMF meetings, said on [USN:L1N4620G5 TEXT:"Friday"] the central bank will focus on anchoring underlying inflation around its 2% target and won't tolerate any overshoot, stressing anew its resolve to continue raising interest rates. For Japan, a weak yen adds to factors pushing up inflation by boosting the cost of raw material imports. Such mounting price pressures prodded the BOJ to raise rates to a 31-year high of 1.25% in [USN:L1N459138 TEXT:"September"], following a hike in June. Many analysts expect another rate increase by year-end. Japan also conducted a rare, coordinated intervention with the US on [USN:L1N43Z05E TEXT:"July 31"] to prevent the currency's slide to near 40-year lows from destabilising financial markets. In staff analysis included in its report on Asia's economy, the IMF said a big portion of yen moves since mid-2025 had little to do with fundamental factors such as yield differentials, and instead co-moved with speculative positions in yen futures. "Japan has a deep foreign exchange market, so as a first line of defense, they have allowed the exchange rate to move," Srinivasan said. "Bottom line, I would say that the Japanese authorities are fully committed to a freely floating exchange rate. I've had many discussions with them. So I don't doubt that at all," he said when asked if the recent yen intervention was justified. FISCAL FRAMEWORK NEEDED Rising global bond yields have also drawn attention at this week's IMF meetings as debt in advanced economies, including Japan, expanded after years of heavy spending. Markets worry that Japan may add to its already huge debt pile with the administration's big spending plans and a two-year cut to the consumption tax from April next year. Srinivasan said Japan has in fact seen fiscal consolidation proceed more than any other G7 country since the pandemic due in part to rising tax revenues. "Markets are concerned about the fiscal risks because of the uncertainty" on how Japan would pay for the fresh spending and tax-cut plans, he said. "Japan also would benefit from having a medium-term fiscal framework."

item.title: Major development banks step up support for critical minerals value chains
item.description: Multilateral development banks (MDBs) will strengthen efforts to help mineral-rich developing economies add more value to their resources by moving beyond extraction into processing, refining and manufacturing, according to an outline of a critical minerals collaboration framework published on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Multilateral development banks (MDBs) will strengthen efforts to help mineral-rich developing economies add more value to their resources by moving beyond extraction into processing, refining and manufacturing, according to an outline of a critical minerals collaboration framework published on Saturday. The banks involved include the World Bank, the African Development Bank, the Asian Development Bank, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, the European Investment Bank and the Inter-American Development Bank, according to the outline The October framework calls for coordinated support across critical mineral supply chains, including financing, infrastructure and policy aimed at creating jobs, boosting domestic value addition, attracting private investment and supporting low-carbon transition MDBs plan to support mineral corridors incorporating power, transport, logistics, water and digital infrastructure, while strengthening project preparation and using co-financing, guarantees and other financing tools to mobilise capital and accelerate private sector investments They will also seek closer alignment on environmental and social standards, coordinate support to governments and better connect mining projects with infrastructure and industrial development An MDB working group will coordinate implementation of the framework's objectives and report annually to the Heads of MDBs Group on progress

item.title: Canada women snap world champion England's 41-match unbeaten run
item.description: Canada’s women snapped world champion England’s 41-match unbeaten run with a 24-21 victory in Toronto on Friday, achieving a goal they have long been working toward.
item.dc:creator: Nicole Fernandes
item.content:encoded: Canada’s women snapped world champion England’s 41-match unbeaten run with a 24-21 victory in Toronto on Friday, achieving a goal they have long been working toward. One month after halting England's 39-match winning streak following a 26-26 draw in Exeter, a late try from Shoshanah Seumanutafa put Canada ahead with less than three minutes left to play. “Definitely special," Canada captain Sophie de Goede told reporters after the landmark win. "I think there were a lot of ups and downs throughout that game and we really had to grind it out and find a way, and that's kind of the DNA of our team and our group. "So, I think more than anything, I feel proud of the way that we found a way to win that game, and it wasn't easy.” The opener of a two-game Rugby Rematch Tour between the growing rivals drew an electric crowd to BMO Field as Canada returned to home soil for the first time since finishing runner-up to the Red Roses at last year's World Cup. "I think it's a little bit more than just the score at the end because we won on so many levels today," Canada's Justine Pelletier said. "Off the field, just the crowd, being home, and there's so much going on around. And I think that win at the end on the pitch was just the cherry on (top)." Savannah Bauder, Alysha Corrigan and DaLeaka Menin also scored tries for Canada, while Maddie Feaunati, Zoe Harrison and Sarah Bern added one each for England. England's unbeaten run had stretched back to their World Cup final defeat by New Zealand in 2022. Canada’s last win over the Red Roses came in 2016 at the Women's Rugby Super Series. “It was good to beat England, but I think for a few years now we knew that we could beat them," Pelletier said. "It was just a matter of time and a matter of putting every detail together." For top-ranked England, having a target on their back is nothing new. “The bit we always remember is we're at the top, and when you're at the top, people want to bring you down as quick as they can,” England captain Megan Jones said, adding that the team take "huge pride" in their unbeaten run. Jones also praised the atmosphere in Toronto, where 18,621 fans rocked the stands all night in chilly conditions, setting an attendance record for a women’s rugby match in North America. "We're the biggest advocates for the game," Jones said of players. "So we're always going to try and grow the game as much as we can, and Canada definitely did that in tenfold today." Canada and England will face off in the second game of the Rugby Rematch Tour on October 23 in Ottawa.

item.title: Nathan MacKinnon’s 4-point night powers Avalanche past Penguins
item.description: Nathan MacKinnon had a goal and three assists to lead the Colorado Avalanche to a 5-2 win over the Pittsburgh Penguins on Friday in Denver.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Nathan MacKinnon had a goal and three assists to lead the Colorado Avalanche to a 5-2 win over the Pittsburgh Penguins on Friday in Denver. Artturi Lehkonen scored twice while Gabriel Landeskog and T.J. Hughes added goals for the Avalanche, who went 2-0-1 while playing three games in four nights. Martin Necas had three assists, Cale Makar added two, and Mackenzie Blackwood made 29 saves. Evgeni Malkin and Bryan Rust got the goals for the Penguins, who are 1-4-1 in their past six. Arturs Silovs turned away 27 shots. Colorado scored the only three goals of the second period to go up 4-2. Lehkonen notched his second goal of the night 25 seconds into the frame, tying it 2-2. He knocked down the rebound of MacKinnon's shot off the goalpost with his glove and scored from the crease. Landeskog gave Colorado the lead for good at 4:24, slamming a Brock Nelson pass into the open side of the net. Hughes scored his first career NHL goal when he tipped in MacKinnon's pass with 5:03 left in the period, four seconds after an Avalanche power play expired. MacKinnon added a power-play goal on a one-timer from just above the left dot with 4:54 left in the third to make it five straight goals for the Avalanche. He has 16 points (six goals and 10 assists) in eight games this season. Silovs stopped MacKinnon's penalty-shot attempt 15 seconds before Landeskog's goal. Pittsburgh jumped ahead 2-0 with two goals 29 seconds apart in the first period. Malkin scored as he cut across the slot after charging down the right wing. He shot as he fell and beat Blackwood 8:28 into the game. Rust then tipped in Sidney Crosby's pass on a 2-on-1 rush at 8:57. Colorado got on the board at 11:01 of the first when Lehkonen tipped in a pass from MacKinnon off the rush. New Avalanche assistant coach Brett McLean made his debut behind the bench after replacing Dave Hakstol, who departed to become the head coach at Arizona State. --Field Level Media

item.title: Carapaz joins NSN on three-year deal
item.description: Former Giro d'Italia winner and Olympic champion Richard Carapaz joined NSN Cycling Team on Friday, after leaving EF Education-EasyPost a year before the end of his contract.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Former Giro d'Italia winner and Olympic champion Richard Carapaz joined NSN Cycling Team on Friday, after leaving EF Education-EasyPost a year before the end of his contract. The 33-year-old Ecuadorean, who won the Giro in 2019 and road race gold at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021, signed a three-year deal with NSN, formerly known as Israel–Premier Tech. "I'm really looking forward to it, and to be honest, this reminds me a lot of when I signed my first professional contract, when I was incredibly excited about being in the WorldTour," Carapaz said in a statement. "The team has big ambitions to keep growing and already in my conversations with the performance team, it was clear we share the same desire to keep improving and achieve big things together." Carapaz, renowned for his climbing ability, won two stages at this year's Tour de France to finish eighth overall.

item.title: Australia confirms first H5N1 bird flu case on sub-Antarctic Macquarie Island
item.description: Australia on Saturday confirmed its first case of H5N1 bird flu on the sub-Antarctic Macquarie Island, with the deadly virus found in the remote territory's vulnerable elephant seal population.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Australia on Saturday confirmed its first case of H5N1 bird flu on the sub-Antarctic Macquarie Island, with the deadly virus found in the remote territory's vulnerable elephant seal population. Australia's Chief Veterinary Officer Beth Cookson said official testing confirmed the highly pathogenic virus strain "in samples collected from an elephant seal and a kelp gull on Macquarie Island, marking the first H5 event on this island". Australia in June became the last continent to report bird flu, although the virus was detected in late 2025 on another of its sub-Antarctic territories, Heard Island, where more than 13,000 baby seals were killed by the virus, according to local media. Like Heard Island, Macquarie Island, a UNESCO World Heritage-listed territory located in the Southern Ocean halfway between Australia's Tasmania state and Antarctica, is a key breeding ground for southern elephant seals. The mammals, which can weigh up to 3,600 kg (7,936 pounds), are particularly susceptible to H5 bird flu, with pup mortality rates in some cases of more than 90%, according to the federal government. In August, Australia's environment department said it would withdraw personnel from a research station on Macquarie Island due to the "psycho-social risk to expeditioners of a potential H5 avian influenza outbreak". Expert assessments predicted the virus would likely cause a significant elephant seal mortality event during the upcoming breeding season, the environment department said.

item.title: Juez mexicano condena a 158 años en prisión a asesinos de surfistas extranjeros
item.description: Un juez mexicano condenó el viernes a tres hombres a 158 años y nueve meses de prisión por el asesinato de dos hermanos australianos y de su amigo estadounidense durante un viaje de surf en 2024 al estado de Baja California, informó una fuente judicial.
item.dc:creator: Lizbeth Diaz, Yolanda Morales
item.content:encoded: Un juez mexicano condenó el viernes a tres hombres a 158 años y nueve meses de prisión por el asesinato de dos hermanos australianos y de su amigo estadounidense durante un viaje de surf en 2024 al estado de Baja California, informó una fuente judicial. La semana pasada el mismo juez [USN:L6N45V14R TEXT:" declaro culpables"] a Jesús Gerardo "N" alias "El Kekas", Irineo Francisco "N" y Ángel Jesús "N" de homicidio y robo calificado cuando se cometa de noche, robo con violencia y robo de vehículo con violencia, en agravio de los hermanos Jake y Callum Robinson así como de su amigo Jack Carter Rhoad. Además de la condena, el juez ordenó el pago de una multa de poco más de un millón de pesos como reparación del daño a la familia de los hermanos Robinson, así como de 549 mil pesos a la familia Carter, dijo una fuente del poder Judicial el estado Baja California. “Desde el fondo de mi corazón, agradezco a todas las personas y a todos los testigos”, dijo por Zoom Page Rhoad, madre del joven estadounidense asesinado, al concluir la audiencia a la que Reuters asistió. "Nunca habrá justicia por perder un hijo, pero estos hombres no volverán a hacer daño a nadie mas", agregó. Los cuerpos de los extranjeros fueron encontrados dentro de un pozo de agua con heridas de bala en la cabeza, días después de que su familia reportara su desaparición en abril de 2024. La camioneta en que viajaban fue localizada calcinada en otro punto, a varios kilómetros de donde ocurrieron los hechos. Aunque Ensenada se considera relativamente segura, Baja California se encuentra entre los estados más violentos de México. Tras los asesinatos, el Departamento de Estado estadounidense instó a sus ciudadanos a reconsiderar viajar a la zona debido a los riesgos de delincuencia y secuestro. El 19 de noviembre, Gisell Silva, entonces novia de "El Kekas", fue condenada a 20 años de prisión por su participación en el caso. La mujer de entonces 23 años fue detenida pocos días después de que fueron encontrados los cadáveres de los extranjeros. Martin y Debra Robinson, padres de Jake y Callum, siguieron la audiencia de sentencia de forma remota tras regresar a Australia la semana pasada, luego de conocer el fallo de culpabilidad. Entrevistados al salir de una de las 24 audiencias que duró el proceso, describieron la muerte de sus hijos como “un infierno” y una experiencia “increíblemente difícil”. La lectura final de la sentencia está programada para el 23 de octubre, dijo la misma fuente del Poder Judicial.

item.title: Rainout forces Guardians, Rays to play ALCS straight through to finish
item.description: CLEVELAND -- Major League Baseball officials did not want to postpone Game 4 of the American League Championship Series, but soaking, day-long rain forced their hand.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: CLEVELAND -- Major League Baseball officials did not want to postpone Game 4 of the American League Championship Series, but soaking, day-long rain forced their hand. As a result, the Cleveland Guardians and Tampa Bay Rays will play the rescheduled contest on Saturday night. Cleveland leads the best-of-seven series 2-1. Guardians right-hander Shawn Armstrong (0-0, 0.00 ERA postseason) takes on Rays right-hander Nick Martinez (0-0, 4.91 ERA postseason). Both were slated to start Friday before the game was called one hour after its scheduled first pitch, but play never began. "It was obviously a long day to wait to not have a game," said Cleveland manager Stephen Vogt, who was visibly and audibly perturbed at his post-rainout press conference. "It's completely out of our control, but this is what happens. "This is baseball. This is Cleveland. We're more than used to these kinds of days." The postponement will force the teams to play the final four games on consecutive days, if needed, with Game 5 in Cleveland on Sunday. The series would return to St. Petersburg, Fla., for Game 6 and Game 7, if necessary. Since the Rays play in a domed stadium and there is no rain in the forecast for Northeast Ohio this weekend, the AL crown will be awarded no later than Tuesday. Temperatures for the next two games are expected to be in the low 40s. "No, I'm not frustrated at all," Tampa Bay manager Kevin Cash said. "I have no reason to be frustrated. We did everything just like we would do during the regular season. There was no guarantee there wasn't another band of rain coming." Armstrong, a former Rays reliever, allowed one hit over 1 2/3 scoreless innings in Game 2. He will serve as the opener, with left-hander Joey Cantillo and right-hander Slade Cecconi likely among those to follow. Armstrong was less fortunate in his previous outing against Tampa Bay, allowing three runs in two-thirds of an inning in a no-decision on July 24. He has a 6.14 ERA in 16 total appearances against the Rays (regular season and postseason), all out of the bullpen. "If you compare both organizations on paper and what they've done, it's a really good battle to have in the ALCS," Armstrong said. "We're thankful to be here. So are they. At the end of the day, I hope we come out on top." Martinez pitched brilliantly against the Guardians during the 2026 regular season, winning both starts while allowing seven hits and one walk over 13 scoreless innings. He added nine strikeouts as Cleveland posted a .159/.178/.182 slash line against him. The 36-year-old Miami native pitched 3 2/3 innings and gave up two runs against the New York Yankees when he started Game 3 of the AL Division Series. Martinez went 15-6 with a 3.10 ERA in 31 regular-season starts this year, but Cash made him a relief option earlier in the ALCS. "The first game, I sat in the bullpen and didn't really like it," Martinez said, chuckling. "I was in the dugout with cleats on the second game. Whatever the team needs, I'm up for it. That's got to be my mentality for the rest of the year." Martinez is 3-2 with a 4.39 ERA in eight career appearances (four starts) against the Guardians. He has pitched in Cleveland twice (one start), throwing nine scoreless innings with five strikeouts while compiling a 1-0 record. --Brian Dulik, Field Level Media

item.title: Boca Juniors remonta ante Talleres y toma el liderato en la tabla anual del fútbol argentino
item.description: Boca Juniors se colocó en la cima de la tabla anual del fútbol argentino al remontar un marcador adverso y vencer el viernes 2-1 como local a Talleres de Córdoba en la decimotercera jornada del Torneo Clausura.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Boca Juniors se colocó en la cima de la tabla anual del fútbol argentino al remontar un marcador adverso y vencer el viernes 2-1 como local a Talleres de Córdoba en la decimotercera jornada del Torneo Clausura. Con este resultado, Boca llegó a 54 puntos en la sumatoria general que también otorga un título de campeón al final de la temporada. Independiente Rivadavia y Argentinos Juniors lo siguen con 52 y 51 unidades, respectivamente. "Siempre es lindo marcar con esta camiseta. Estamos muy contentos por el triunfo del equipo. Sabíamos que hoy teníamos que ganar para quedar arriba en la tabla", dijo el uruguayo Miguel Merentiel a la televisión local. En el partido disputado en el estadio La Bombonera, Talleres abrió el marcador a los 11 minutos con un remate de larga distancia de Matías Galarza que sorprendió al arquero colombiano Álvaro Montero. Merentiel anotó el empate para Boca a los 18 minutos con una definición precisa tras una asistencia de Lautaro Blanco. El segundo gol de Boca llegó a los 49 minutos por intermedio del joven Leonel Flores luego de una gran jugada individual y un remate cruzado. "Nos vamos con sensaciones tristes, porque no conseguimos el resultado que vinimos a buscar, pero hicimos un buen partido frente a un rival de mucha jerarquía", indicó Galarza tras la derrota. Por su parte, Instituto de Córdoba mantuvo el liderato de la Zona A al vencer 1-0 de visitante a Defensa y Justicia con un gol de Jeremías Lázaro a los 23 minutos. Instituto llegó a 29 puntos en la tabla de posiciones, cinco por encima de Defensa y Justicia y Boca Juniors. La jornada comenzó el jueves con el triunfo 2-1 de Gimnasia y Esgrima La Plata sobre Huracán.

item.title: Striking unions at Antofagasta's Centinela copper mine reach preliminary deal, ending strike
item.description: Workers from two striking unions at Antofagasta's Centinela copper mine in Chile reached a preliminary agreement on a new collective contract, ending a strike that has lasted more than a week at the mine, the unions said late on Friday in a statement sent to its members.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Workers from two striking unions at Antofagasta's (ANTO.L) Centinela copper mine in Chile reached a preliminary agreement on a new collective contract, ending a strike that has lasted more than a week at the mine, the unions said late on Friday in a statement sent to its members. The unions called a meeting on Friday night to present the agreement to members and a vote to ratify it will be held on Saturday. The more than 700 members of Distrito Centinela and Minera Esperanza unions [USN:L1N45T0DW TEXT:"began the strike"] on October 7 after contract talks failed. They had demanded that workers have the same benefits regardless of the union they belong to. The unions returned to the negotiating table this week to find a resolution to the conflict. Three striking workers had also been on a hunger strike since October 9 to pressure the parties into reaching a solution to the stalled talks. Antofagasta said it had presented the striking unions with new proposals covering key issues and offering a significant improvement in economic terms. The strike at Centinela, along with the [USN:L1N4600CR TEXT:"threat of a strike"] at BHP’s Escondida mine in Chile, has been supporting global copper prices amid fears that it would be difficult to boost supply to meet projected future demand. Antofagasta said this week it has managed to [USN:S0N44M02N TEXT:"maintain production"] at normal levels, avoiding the negative effects of the work stoppage. In 2025, Centinela produced 240,400 metric tons of copper.

item.title: Trabajadores de mina chilena Centinela logran preacuerdo con Antofagasta para nuevo contrato y terminar huelga: sindicato
item.description: Los trabajadores de dos sindicatos en huelga de la mina chilena de cobre Centinela lograron un preacuerdo con Antofagasta Minerals para un nuevo contrato colectivo, lo que permitiría terminar la paralización de más de una semana, dijeron el viernes los gremios en un informativo enviado a sus socios.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Los trabajadores de dos sindicatos en huelga de la mina chilena de cobre Centinela lograron un preacuerdo con Antofagasta Minerals para un nuevo contrato colectivo, lo que permitiría terminar la paralización de más de una semana, dijeron el viernes los gremios en un informativo enviado a sus socios. Los sindicatos Distrito Centinela y Minera Esperanza convocaron a una asamblea la noche del viernes para presentar el acuerdo, que será sometido a un voto de ratificación por los socios el sábado. Los más de 700 agremiados iniciaron la detención el 7 de octubre tras fracasar el diálogo contractual, donde pedían que los trabajadores tengan los mismos beneficios independiente del sindicato al pertenezcan. Pero esta semana volvieron a la mesa de diálogo en un intento por encontrar una salida al conflicto. En tanto, tres trabajadores mantenían una huelga de hambre en un intento por presionar una solución a las estancadas conversaciones entre las partes. Antofagasta afirmó en la semana que ha logrado sostener su producción en niveles normales lo que evitado los efectos negativos de la paralización. En 2025, Centinela produjo 240.400 toneladas de cobre. Además argumentó que durante esta semana había presentado nuevas propuestas con materias relevantes y una mejora significativa en las condiciones económicas. La huelga en Centinela, además del riesgo finalmente no consumado de paralización de supervisores en Escondida, de BHP, ha estado apoyando los precios globales del cobre en medio de los temores sobre la dificultad de impulsar la oferta para abastecer el consumo estimado hacia adelante.

item.title: Hacker gets data on millions of California students, state education department says
item.description: The California Department of Education said on Friday a hacker accessed the data of millions of students, including names, birth dates, addresses and disability status, by exploiting the system of a non-profit contractor that works with the state.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The California Department of Education said on Friday a hacker accessed the data of millions of students, including names, birth dates, addresses and disability status, by exploiting the system of a non-profit contractor that works with the state. The hacker accessed the data of "all students enrolled in the three previous school years," the department said. More than 5.7 million students were enrolled in California during the 2025-2026 school year, according to the department. The non-profit, Educational Testing Service, on Friday began notifying students and their families of the breach, which was identified late last month but found to have been ongoing since May, the education department said. The non-profit identified the breach involving a secure file transfer protocol site on September 25 and began an investigation, according to the California agency. "The investigation determined that an unauthorized party used a compromised login credential to access the site and copy files containing California student information at various times between May 22 and September 18, 2026," the education department said. Educational Testing Service has not found that any of the information has been made public so far, the education department said, adding that Social Security numbers and sensitive financial information were not accessed. In an October 2 letter to county and district school officials, the California agency said the testing service had stopped "normal enrollment data processing." "The CDE is actively working to minimize disruption and resume affected assessment activities in a timely manner," the department said. In California, Educational Testing Service administers statewide assessments including those for English language proficiency. "We have implemented additional safeguards, including enhanced monitoring, strengthened access controls, and further third-party review of our security practices," Educational Testing Service said in a statement to Reuters. "Our priority remains the students, families and educators we serve and safeguarding the assessment programs we deliver for our clients and partners globally."

item.title: Three sentenced to 158 years in Mexico for murder of Australian, US surfers
item.description: A Mexican judge on Friday sentenced three men to 158 years and nine months in prison each for the killings of two Australian brothers and their American friend during a 2024 surf trip to the state of Baja California, a judicial official said.
item.dc:creator: Lizbeth Diaz, Yolanda Morales
item.content:encoded: A Mexican judge on Friday sentenced three men to 158 years and nine months in prison each for the killings of two Australian brothers and their American friend during a 2024 surf trip to the state of Baja California, a judicial official said. The defendants, identified by authorities simply as Jesus Gerardo "N," known as "El Kekas," Irineo Francisco "N" and Angel Jesus "N," were [USN:L6N45V14M TEXT:"found guilty"] a week ago of homicide, aggravated robbery, robbery with violence and vehicle theft with violence. The victims were Australian brothers Jake Robinson, 33, and Callum Robinson, 30, and their American friend Jack Carter Rhoad, 30. The judge also ordered the defendants to pay compensation to the victims' families, said an official from the Baja California state judiciary. In November, Gisell Silva was sentenced to 20 years in prison after pleading guilty to aggravated robbery with violence and vehicle theft with violence, in a fast-track proceeding. The woman, then 23, was arrested a few days after the foreigners’ bodies were found in a water well. The Robinson brothers and Rhoad were camping and surfing near Punta San Jose, about 80 km (50 miles) south of Ensenada, when they were reported missing in late April 2024. After a days-long search, aided by the FBI, their bodies were found on May 3 at the bottom of a well. The victims were each found with gunshot wounds to the head, and the pickup truck they were traveling in was found, burned, several kilometers away, authorities said. “There will never be justice for the loss of a child, but these men will never hurt anyone else again,” said Page Rhoad, mother of the slain American, via Zoom after the sentencing. Martin and Debra Robinson, parents of Jake and Callum, followed the sentencing hearing remotely after returning to Australia last week, following the initial guilty verdict. In an interview as they left one of the 24 hearings that made up the trial, they described their sons’ deaths as “hell” and an “incredibly difficult” experience. While the Ensenada area is considered relatively safe, Baja California ranks among Mexico’s most violent states. Following the killings, the US State Department urged Americans to reconsider travel to the state due to crime and kidnapping risks. ($1 = 18.4810 Mexican pesos)

item.title: Brazil's Flavio Bolsonaro pledges fiscal adjustment, rejects cuts to social spending
item.description: Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro said on Friday that, if elected president, he would seek to curb Brazil's rising public debt without touching politically sensitive social spending commitments, rejecting media reports that his campaign was considering such measures.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro said on Friday that, if elected president, he would seek to curb Brazil's rising public debt without touching politically sensitive social spending commitments, rejecting media reports that his campaign was considering such measures. The right-wing lawmaker, the eldest son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, will face leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in a runoff on October 25 and [USN:L1N461163 TEXT:"currently leads"] polls against the incumbent. In an interview with TV Globo's Jornal Nacional, the most-watched newscast in Brazil, Bolsonaro pledged to deliver a 200 billion real ($39.49 billion) fiscal adjustment in the federal budget if elected Bolsonaro dismissed proposals attributed by media reports to his campaign to halt real minimum wage increases, eliminate automatic adjustments for social benefits or reduce mandatory social expenditures "There has been a lot of fake news circulating, and this is an important moment to set the record straight," the senator said Instead, Bolsonaro said the adjustment would come from eliminating ministries, tackling mismanagement at state-controlled firms and monetizing federal real estate assets Brazil's gross debt has risen more than 10 percentage points during Lula's term to 82.9% of GDP, while long-term interest rates have fallen since Bolsonaro's [USN:L6N45Q04L TEXT:"first-round victory"] The senator also said he would not seek to reverse a constitutional amendment [USN:L1N46100U TEXT:"approved on Wednesday"] to shorten the working week in Brazil from six to five days ($1 = 5.0648 reais)

item.title: Trump threatens California officials with imprisonment over stance on mail ballots
item.description: The Justice Dept. said election officials could be liable as abettors of a federal crime.
item.dc:creator: Jasper Ward
item.content:encoded: The US Justice Department on Friday warned Los Angeles County and California election officials they could be liable as abettors of a federal crime if they count mail ballots returned by more than 20,000 people the Trump administration says are probably noncitizens. The warning to the Los Angeles County Assistant Counsel Peter Bollinger came less than three weeks before the November 3 midterm elections and days after the department gave California [USN:L6N460192 TEXT:"48 hours"] to review a list of alleged noncitizen voters or face legal action. On Thursday, the Justice Department [USN:L6N46117W TEXT:"sued California"] to block the state from counting the ballots. "Noncitizen voting in a federal election is a federal crime — and knowingly facilitating such conduct is equally unlawful," Trent McCotter, the acting US deputy attorney general, wrote in a letter released on Friday. McCotter called on the county and California's secretary of state to reconsider their refusal to take steps that the Trump administration argues are needed to deter voter fraud. US President Donald Trump shared the letter on Truth Social with the comment: "They will all go to jail for a long period of time!!!" California Secretary of State Shirley Weber and Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder Dean Logan were copied on McCotter's letter. The county's counsel office did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Weber's office referred Reuters to an earlier statement in which she said the Justice Department's attempts to "unlawfully gain access to states' protected voter data and purge voter rolls serve only to cause chaos and fuel public distrust in our elections." An earlier letter that McCotter sent on Tuesday to Weber and Logan said the Justice Department provided officials in Los Angeles County with a "password-protected thumb drive" with the names of people the federal government "believes are likely noncitizens" that were sent mail-in ballots from California. Los Angeles County Counsel Dawyn R. Harrison said on Thursday the county cannot comply with the Justice Department's requests because the Trump administration did not explain how the list was made. Friday's letter from McCotter said the Justice Department used "internal immigration records" and data matching. In July, Trump said his administration had uncovered [USN:L1N43I0TJ TEXT:"evidence"] of more than 275,000 non-citizens registered to vote, but it was not clear how many had actually voted. In some previous cases, systems intended to verify citizenship have mistakenly flagged some naturalized US citizens as noncitizens. Studies have found that noncitizens casting actual ballots is exceedingly uncommon. Since July, the Justice Department has [USN:L6N45F10R TEXT:"ramped up prosecutions"] of people accused of illegally voting while not holding US citizenship. The White House has also [USN:L6N45D0T4 TEXT:"pushed"] federal agencies to accelerate their review of at least 47 state voter rolls obtained by the Department of Homeland Security, according to an internal email seen by Reuters.

item.title: India's 'cockroach' movement founder released a day after detention
item.description: India's "cockroach" youth movement leader was released by an Indian court on Saturday, a day after he was detained for trying to lead another protest rally in New Delhi calling for the resignation of the country's election chief.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: India's "cockroach" youth movement leader was released by an Indian court on Saturday, a day after he was detained for trying to lead another protest rally in New Delhi calling for the resignation of the country's election chief. Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), rose to prominence this year when a weeks-long sit-in contributed to India's education minister resigning. CJP's legal affairs head Ratna Singh said Dipke was released after he agreed to certain conditions. Singh gave no details of the terms. Dipke's youth-led group, opposition parties and student organisations have held near-daily protests this month demanding Chief Election Commissioner [USN:P8N44T0DC TEXT:"Gyanesh Kumar's"] resignation over a revision of [USN:L1N45V037 TEXT:"voter lists"] that they say favours Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). More than 130 million voters were deleted during the revision. The Election Commission has denied favouring any party and said wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol. The BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes. Student activist Neha Bora, a prominent face of the protests, who was also detained on Friday as she tried to reach central Delhi with dozens of supporters, was released on Saturday. "Please, spare the people of India. Impeach Gyanesh Kumar and halt SIR (special intensive revision), so that the ordinary citizens of this country can breathe a sigh of relief, feel at ease, and have their voting rights ensured," Bora told ANI news agency after she was released. STUDENT GROUPS CALL FOR MORE PROTEST ACTION Dipke was [USN:L6N4620GJ TEXT:"detained"] on Friday as he stepped out of a house in central Delhi, with police hauling him into a police car and driving away after a brief argument. Dipke had called Friday's protest in support of two CJP leaders detained and sent to jail this week for five days for demonstrating at a protest site in violation of a ban. Earlier on Friday, police had met Dipke and warned him against going ahead with the protest. Student groups called for more protest action on Saturday. The movement, which was mobilised by the youth and joined by many opposition parties, has emerged as one of the biggest political challenges faced by Modi and the BJP in the prime minister's 12 years in power.

item.title: USA-Trump lève des sanctions liées à la Russie avant leur entrée en vigueur
item.description: Le président américain Donald Trump a annoncé vendredi la levée de plusieurs sanctions, restrictions et droits de douane visant la Russie, prévus dans le cadre d'une loi promulguée le mois dernier, avant leur entrée en vigueur.
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh, Jasper Ward
item.content:encoded: Le président américain Donald Trump a annoncé vendredi la levée de plusieurs sanctions, restrictions et droits de douane visant la Russie, prévus dans le cadre d'une loi promulguée le mois dernier, avant leur entrée en vigueur. Donald Trump a [USN:L6N45A18I TEXT:"promulgué"] en septembre le "Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026", une législation qui vise les secteurs de l'énergie et de la défense russes, ainsi que la "flotte fantôme" de pétroliers qui contournent les sanctions existantes, afin de priver Moscou des fonds nécessaires au financement de sa guerre contre l'Ukraine. "J'ai transmis au Congrès une attestation indiquant que l'octroi d'une telle dérogation à l'heure actuelle sert les intérêts nationaux des Etats-Unis", a indiqué Donald Trump dans un décret publié vendredi par la Maison blanche. La publication de ce décret intervient alors que Donald Trump a publiquement critiqué le président ukrainien, Volodimir Zelensky et a annoncé un [USN:L8N45V1O6 TEXT:"accord"], conclu entre Washington et Moscou, concernant l'approvisionnement en diesel. Cet accord entraîne la levée de sanctions américaines contre les exportations de diesel russe afin de permettre à Moscou de fournir dans un premier temps près de deux millions de tonnes de gazole aux Etats-Unis et sur les marchés mondiaux.

item.title: Stephen Ross sells minority Dolphins stake at NFL-record valuation
item.description: Miami Dolphins principal owner Stephen Ross agreed to sell another minority stake in the team and its affiliated businesses, continuing a series of transactions dating to December 2024.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Miami Dolphins principal owner Stephen Ross agreed to sell another minority stake in the team and its affiliated businesses, continuing a series of transactions dating to December 2024. First reported by Sports Business Journal on Friday, Ross agreed to sell 2.1% of the Dolphins, along with pieces of Hard Rock Stadium, the F1 Hard Rock Miami Grand Prix, and the organization's interest in the Miami Open tennis event, to Chilean billionaire financier Jean Eric Salata. Salata, worth $8.4 billion according to Forbes, will reportedly acquire the stake at a valuation slightly above $12.5 billion. In March, Ross sold 1% of the club to Xiaomi co-founder Lin Bin for a valuation of $12.5 billion. Lin Bin was born in China but is a U.S. citizen. That equity sale established a record high for NFL minority stakes. Salata, 60, was born in Chile and founded Baring Private Equity Asia in Hong Kong. The firm was acquired in 2022 by Swedish investment giant EQT AB, which Salata now chairs. Salata and his family moved to Erie, Pa., when he was five years old. He earned a bachelor's degree from Penn and worked for Bain & Co. in Boston. Ross sold 10% of the team to Ares Management and a combined 3% stake to Brooklyn Nets principal owner Joe Tsai and minority owner Oliver Weisberg in December 2024. Those deals valued the Dolphins at $8.1 billion. The team's standalone enterprise value is estimated at $10.59 billion, based on the average of public valuations compiled by SBJ research. The NFL's finance committee approved the transaction last month, and league owners are expected to formally approve the sale at their meeting next week in New York. --Field Level Media

item.title: Flávio diz que não irá trabalhar para reverter fim da 6x1 e garante manter reajuste do mínimo e aposentadorias
item.description: O senador e candidato à Presidência Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) afirmou nesta sexta-feira em entrevista à TV Globo que não irá trabalhar para reverter o fim da escala de trabalho conhecida como 6x1.
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Brito, Maria Marcello
item.content:encoded: O senador e candidato à Presidência Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) afirmou nesta sexta-feira em entrevista à TV Globo que não irá trabalhar para reverter o fim da escala de trabalho conhecida como 6x1. Flávio, que disputa o segundo turno da eleição presidencial com o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), era contra a mudança na escala de trabalho, mas acabou mudando de posição diante do apoio popular e do crescimento do apoio à medida no Senado. Uma das principais bandeiras do petista à reeleição, a Proposta de Emenda à Constituição (PEC) foi aprovada na quarta-feira pelo Senado e promulgada na manhã desta sexta em sessão que contou com a presença do próprio Lula. "Não vou... é importante a sua pergunta, todos os direitos trabalhistas estão garantidos. Cada um pode ter sua opinião individual, mas da minha parte isso aqui está respeitado, foi uma decisão do Congresso Nacional. Então da minha parte nenhum questionamento com relação a isso", ressaltou. Flávio disse que mudou de posição sobre a proposta após ouvir a população brasileira durante a campanha. AJUSTE FISCAL Na entrevista, o candidato também garantiu que irá manter os reajustes do salário mínimo acima da inflação, que não irá desvincular o percentual de reajuste de aposentadorias e ainda que não irá eliminar os pisos constitucionais de repasses à saúde e à educação. Uma eventual mexida nesses três pontos é apontada por economistas como necessária para um ajuste fiscal para reduzir a trajetória de endividamento público brasileiro. Dado divulgado pelo Banco Central no fim de setembro aponta que a dívida bruta do Brasil subiu a 82,9% do PIB em agosto. Interlocutores de Flávio Bolsonaro na área econômica dizem que ele poderia fazer um ajuste de até R$250 bilhões para alterar a trajetória da dívida. Na entrevista, o candidato disse que buscará cortar despesas possíveis e buscar novas fontes de receita. Citou que cortaria pelo menos 10 dos atuais 39 ministérios, o que ele próprio admite não teria grande impacto fiscal. Além disso, afirmou que buscará acabar com o que chamou de "corrupção" nas estatais para que elas voltem a ser superavitárias. Mesmo sem detalhar, o senador também defendeu medidas como a eventual securitização de imóveis federais, que estariam avaliados em R$1,7 trilhão, e também a securitização das dívidas que a União tem a receber. "O maior ajuste fiscal que o Brasil pode fazer é tirar o Lula", disse, acrescentando um compromisso de não fazer economia com as pessoas mais pobres e de não atacar o funcionalismo público. Ao contrário de Lula, que preferiu evitar críticas ao adversário na entrevista da véspera, Flávio Bolsonaro atacou em diversas ocasiões o presidente em suas declarações, muitas vezes até quando não respondia aos questionamentos feitos. Questionado se a medida poderia implicar em outros cargos eletivos como parlamentares e governadores ou mesmo a ampliação do mandato presidencial, o senador afirmou que isso vai depender do debate no Congresso Nacional. O candidato disse que, se eleito, seu irmão que está nos Estados Unidos, o ex-deputado Eduardo Bolsonaro, não vai ser chanceler. Entretanto, ele não foi claro sobre qual papel o pai, o ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro, teria no seu governo caso venha a ser eleito. "Não está no radar", afirmou, referindo-se à possibilidade de um cargo ao ex-presidente. "O presidente Bolsonaro nunca tratou de cargo comigo, tenho o privilégio de na hora que tiver que consultar, vou falar com ele", declarou, em outro momento. O senador aproveitou para defender que a condenação de seu pai por tentativa de golpe de Estado pelo Supremo Tribunal Federal foi uma "farsa", conduzida por seus inimigos, citando, entre outros, o ministro Alexandre de Moraes, e que há vários vícios no processo. O candidato, no entanto, afirmou que vai respeitar o resultado da eleição, caso perca a disputa final no próximo dia 25 para Lula. O senador é investigado pela PF por supostos crimes de corrupção, lavagem de dinheiro e evasão de divisas no caso dos repasses feitos por Vorcaro para financiar o filme "Dark Horse". Nesta sexta, a PF pediu a prorrogação das investigações por mais 90 dias, iniciativa essa que está pendente de uma decisão do STF.

item.title: Trump waives key Russia-related sanctions, tariffs before they take effect under new law
item.description: The measures included penalties for buying Russian oil and gas.
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh, Jasper Ward
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump waived key Russia-related US sanctions and tariffs days before they were to take effect under a law he signed last month, including duties on the country's goods and penalties for buying its oil and gas. In an executive order released by the White House on Friday, Trump said the waiver was in the national interests of the United States. The law is meant to increase pressure on Russia for its invasion of Ukraine that began in 2022. Trump, however, has been warming toward Moscow while publicly criticizing Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, including suggesting Kyiv needs a new leader. Zelenskiy, in a message posted on X on Saturday, said Trump's latest action emboldens Russian President Vladimir Putin . "A US sanctions blackout, easing pressure on the aggressor, financial rewards for Putin – all of this only encourages him to keep attacking. We must not give up ground," wrote Zelenskiy, who said Russia on Friday struck more than 15 Ukrainian power generation and transmission sites. "We must keep trying to end the war. To end it, not give Putin every reason to continue it indefinitely." Weeks before [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"US midterm elections"] in which Trump's Republicans are battling to maintain their narrow grip on both chambers of Congress, the new measures could have risked further [USN:L6N45A18J TEXT:"raising oil prices"] as Americans face increased costs largely attributed to the US-Israeli war on Iran, analysts have said. The [USN:L6N45A18J TEXT:"legislation,"] whose primary backer in Congress was the late Senator Lindsey Graham, a South Carolina Republican, would have imposed tariffs of up to 100% within 30 days on all goods brought into the US from the five largest importers of Russian crude oil or gas, as well as any country that knowingly bought oil or gas 30 days after the law was enacted or was among the top five countries helping Russia evade sanctions. The order said the waiver will remain in effect until Trump or his top officials determine that "further action is appropriate." Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 in mid-September. "I have submitted to the Congress a certification that the issuance of such a waiver at this time is in the national interests of the United States," Trump said in the order. Countries such as China and [USN:L1N45G03K TEXT:"India"], which are among the biggest buyers of Russian oil, have raised concerns about the Russia sanctions bill. Beijing has said it "consistently opposed long-arm jurisdiction that lacks a basis in international law" while India warned Washington that new tariffs could impact bilateral ties. The law allows the president to waive sanctions simply by informing Congress that he has determined that they are not in the national interest. US Representative Don Beyer, a Virginia Democrat, blasted Trump for the waiver, saying he was giving in to Putin. "Trump's latest surrender to Putin again betrays our Ukrainian partners and defies clear congressional intent of legislation designed to punish Russia for its illegal war of aggression," Beyer said in a statement. Trump had also faced criticism from several US senators, including some Republicans, over a recent diesel deal with Russia in which Trump agreed to lift sanctions on Russian exports and Russia agreed to supply diesel to global markets in an effort to lower fuel prices. The lawmakers who criticized the deal said it would help fund Russia's war efforts. Putin's investment envoy, Kirill Dmitriev, called Trump's waiver "a truly historic moment," posting on X that the legislation could have effectively brought all economic cooperation between Russia and the US to a halt.

item.title: Bangladesh is battling measles. It's a 'real warning' to other nations
item.description: Bangladesh's vaccination program was a success story until it faltered because of political turmoil. Its unvaccinated children are paying the price.
item.dc:creator: Ruma Paul, Jennifer Rigby, Sam Jahan, Zia Chowdhury
item.content:encoded: Bangladesh is battling to contain the [USN:L4N44Z0Q9 TEXT:"world’s worst measles outbreak"], a crisis exacerbated by weak data, inadequate outreach and vaccination gaps that experts say offers a warning to other nations about the deadly risk of falling immunisation rates. Bangladesh, whose routine vaccination programme faltered in 2025, reported 202,000 suspected measles cases – 22,000 of them laboratory-confirmed – since the start of the outbreak in mid-March to October 9, the World Health Organization said. That’s more suspected cases than any other country this year. So far, 1,147 people have died of the highly contagious disease, with 94% of reported deaths among children under five years old, the WHO said. Bangladesh's experience shows the challenge of containing an outbreak when vaccination coverage falls below 95%, a level the WHO says is needed to prevent outbreaks. Bangladesh almost achieved that in recent years but in 2025 coverage dropped. A Reuters review of WHO documents, alongside interviews with more than a dozen scientists, health workers and officials, shows Bangladesh was also hampered in its emergency response by data that left out millions of children, shortcomings in preparation and a failure to reach enough parents. "This is a real warning to every country," said Mark Jit, a WHO vaccine adviser and professor at the School of Global Public Health at New York University. Preventing an outbreak through vaccinations was easier, cheaper and safer than [USN:L6N45R13M TEXT:"responding to an emergency"], he said. "The response will stop the outbreak eventually, but in the meantime, many will have had measles, and some will have died," he said. Ziauddin Hyder, special assistant on health affairs to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, told Reuters in September the government was doing everything it could to end the outbreak. The government did not respond to further questions sent in October for this article. ‘THEY CAME ONLY AFTER I BURIED MY SON’ In the northeast Sylhet region, one of the worst-hit areas in the nation of 178 million people, two-year-old Arman Hossain died unvaccinated in July, 24 hours after admission to hospital for treatment paid for by selling the family's three-wheeled auto rickshaw. His unvaccinated four-year-old sister survived. His father Amin Mia, 26, said no health workers came to their remote village in Sylhet to offer vaccinations in time. "They came only after I buried my son," he said. Measles usually kills two or three people in every 1,000 cases, the WHO says, but the disease can be more deadly in poorer nations because of factors such as malnutrition. In the town of Chhatak, also in the Sylhet region, the daughter of 30-year-old carpenter Humayun Rashid died unvaccinated in June aged nine months. Labiba Akter could have received an inoculation in April when an emergency programme lowered the vaccination age to six months from nine. "No health worker came to tell us," her father said. In May, Health Minister Sardar Md. Sakhawat Husain said the emergency drive had brought cases in hotspots "almost to zero" and the outbreak was under control. Yet in September, Bangladesh reported a daily average of 1,198 new cases of measles, which causes a high fever, cough and telltale rash. That was the highest total since May. The Bangladesh outbreak comes as [USN:L6N4560OS TEXT:"vaccine hesitancy is rising"], particularly in wealthier nations, amid skepticism championed by figures such as US Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr . In Bangladesh, access to inoculations and awareness are bigger hurdles, experts said. Until recently, Bangladesh had been a vaccination success story. The WHO and the United Nations children’s agency UNICEF estimated that in 2024 it achieved 96% coverage for the first vaccine dose and 93% for the second, which is given to capture the small percentage of children who don't develop immunity after one shot. But that same year, protests erupted that ended 15 years of rule by Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. In the ensuing political turmoil, health workers went on strike, vaccine orders were delayed and follow-up vaccinations that usually accompany routine programmes were disrupted. In a report published in July this year, WHO and UNICEF estimated first-dose coverage in 2025 had fallen to 90%, while second-dose coverage was 86%, several percentage points below the 95% needed for herd immunity. The report also raised questions about the quality of official data on vaccinations for measles and other diseases for the years 2023 to 2025. It said preliminary figures sometimes showed numbers of those inoculated exceeded 100% of those targeted, indicating mistakes in counting doses or target numbers. EMERGENCY PROGRAMME MISSED MILLIONS Still, when the measles outbreak erupted, Bangladesh responded swiftly and initially seemed to be winning the battle. An emergency programme was followed by an initial slowdown in new cases after almost 20 million children received a vaccination in April and May. The government said it had covered every child in the target age group of six months to five years. But in reality the programme fell short. This emerged when another routine health intervention in June had a target list with 4 million more children than the measles campaign despite covering the same age group. "There is a gap," prime ministerial adviser Hyder told Reuters on September 14, as measles cases rose again, blaming vaccine hesitancy by parents or child illnesses for keeping kids away. Other challenges have also emerged. Documents detailing meetings in April and August between the government, the WHO and other health partners, reviewed by Reuters and not previously reported, show how efforts to act fast may have led to shortcomings. Minutes from the April 19 meeting outlined how the government opted for just one round of so-called readiness checks before launching its emergency vaccination programme due to time constraints, instead of the typical four rounds. Checks cover everything from ensuring fridges are available for keeping vaccines cool to determining how many children should be vaccinated. The single round of checks suggested most - but not all - districts were ready, according to the minutes. THE POOREST ‘PAY THE PRICE’ "When preparedness checks are not done properly, it is often the poorest and hardest-to-reach children who miss out on vaccination and pay the price," said Professor Mahmudur Rahman, an epidemiologist and chair of Bangladesh's National Verification Committee for Measles and Rubella Elimination. Hyder said the April campaign was launched in four weeks. Yet Tajul Islam Abdul Bari, who led immunisation in Bangladesh until 2017, said campaigns usually demand months of planning. By the August meeting, shortcomings in the rollout were identified. Minutes noted the proportion of children with confirmed measles cases who had not been vaccinated was "virtually unchanged between pre-campaign (82%) and post-campaign (85%) ... underscoring persistent coverage gaps". The WHO did not respond to questions about the April and August meetings. But deputy WHO representative to Bangladesh, Dr Rajesh Narwal, said the WHO was determined to support the government in its goal of vaccinating every child at risk. "Routine immunisation must become more effective and resilient so that these gaps do not develop again," he said. In Sylhet, where official records show 180 children have died, 8 of 16 families Reuters interviewed in September said they had not seen health workers offering vaccinations. At least six families said health workers visited only after a child had died from measles in their community. At the end of September, the government launched a new campaign to target 3.4 million children previously missed. "We will involve people across villages so that no child is left behind," the health minister told a news conference. Yet reaching every child remains a challenge. UNICEF and the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics say as many as 40% of children go unregistered, while government data showed around a third of health worker posts are unfilled. Health experts are also pushing the government to expand the programme to vaccinate children over five. That age group represents a third of measles cases, the WHO says. In addition, scientists in Bangladesh are studying why immunity is waning faster than expected in babies up to six months or so. They are usually still protected by maternal antibodies, experts say. Ensuring prompt medical care is vital, the WHO says, another challenge for Bangladesh as it also fights a [USN:L4N45N0BI TEXT:"dengue epidemic"]. In September, every ward in Sylhet's 100-bed Shahid Shamsuddin Ahmed Hospital, which is treating measles, appeared overwhelmed. On the day Reuters visited, 178 patients were admitted.

item.title: ALCS Game 4 between Guardians, Rays postponed to Saturday
item.description: CLEVELAND -- Day-long rain that turned into soaking showers in the early evening led to the postponement of Game 4 of the American League Championship Series on Friday night.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: CLEVELAND -- Day-long rain that turned into soaking showers in the early evening led to the postponement of Game 4 of the American League Championship Series on Friday night. The Cleveland Guardians lead the Tampa Bay Rays 2-1 in the best-of-seven series, which now will resume Saturday at 8 p.m. A scheduled off-day Sunday has been erased with Game 5 shifted to 5 p.m. that day, also in Cleveland. MLB officials made the decision to postpone the game an hour after its scheduled first pitch of 8:08 p.m. More than a dozen Rays players were working out in the outfield, playing catch in the heavy rain, before the announcement was made. Rays right-hander Nick Martinez (0-0, 4.91 ERA) was scheduled to pitch against Guardians right-hander Shawn Armstrong (0-0, 0.00 ERA). Cleveland had planned on a bullpen game in order to allow Foster Griffin, Parker Messick and ace Gavin Williams to start the final three potential contests. Games 6 and 7 will be hosted by the Rays. It was the latest weather-related disruption to the championship series. Game 3 on Thursday was moved up from an evening start to 1 p.m. due to inclement weather in the forecast. The Guardians prevailed 3-2 to move ahead in the series. --Brian Dulik, Field Level Media
